content_units: Hope After Crisis Festival Overview
A 3-day program for   2026-09-18 to 2026-09-20   built around recovery, resilience, and renewed connection.

The lineup meets your brief with   9 total films  :   3 dramas, 2 documentaries, 2 animated films, 1 comedy, 1 international feature  , all   140 minutes or under  , and   no more than one black-and-white title  .
3-Day Screening Schedule
Date   Time   Film   Type   Runtime   Why it fits this slot

2026-09-18   2:00 PM     Marcel the Shell with Shoes On     Animated   90 min   A warm, witty opener that immediately invites the audience into the theme through tenderness and small-scale resilience.
2026-09-18   5:00 PM     Leave No Trace     Drama   109 min   The emotional weight deepens here with a quiet, humane portrait of instability, survival, and fragile rebuilding.
2026-09-18   8:00 PM     Hunt for the Wilderpeople     Comedy   101 min   Ends day one with buoyant energy, emotional release, and a hopeful sense of found family.
2026-09-19   1:30 PM     The Secret of Kells     Animated   75 min   A visually inviting start to day two, using art, imagination, and cultural continuity to draw viewers in gently.

2026-09-19   4:00 PM     Collective     Documentary / International feature   109 min   The heaviest slot of the festival: a gripping look at systemic crisis, public grief, and truth-seeking after disaster.
2026-09-19   7:30 PM     The Peanut Butter Falcon     Drama   97 min   Closes with movement, humor, and emotional uplift, turning hardship into momentum and possibility.
2026-09-20   1:30 PM     Won’t You Be My Neighbor?     Documentary   94 min   A welcoming final-day opener that reconnects the audience with compassion, care, and civic hope.
2026-09-20   4:00 PM     The Road     Drama   111 min   The darkest middle slot, confronting crisis directly so the final film can feel genuinely earned.
2026-09-20   7:30 PM     Cinema Paradiso     International feature   124 min   A deeply emotional but life-affirming finale about memory, community, and love of art—energizing in a reflective way.
Programming Rationale by Day
Day 1 — Personal resilience and found family
Marcel the Shell with Shoes On
- Opens accessibly for a mixed 18+ audience with humor, charm, and emotional immediacy.
- Its intimate scale makes the festival theme feel personal rather than abstract.
Leave No Trace
- Provides the heavier center with realism and emotional depth.
- Examines crisis without sensationalism, keeping the audience engaged rather than overwhelmed.
Hunt for the Wilderpeople
- Sends people out energized through laughter, adventure, and mutual care.
- Its upbeat tone prevents the first day from ending in emotional exhaustion.
Day 2 — Collective trauma, truth, and forward motion
The Secret of Kells
- Starts the day with beauty and mythic imagination.
- Offers a lighter entry point while still connecting to cultural survival and creative hope.
Collective
- Ideal as the centerpiece because it is urgent, morally serious, and intellectually gripping.
- It embodies “after crisis” through accountability, journalism, and civic courage.
The Peanut Butter Falcon
- Restores lift after the documentary’s intensity.
- Its adventurous warmth and accessible humor make it an excellent crowd-pleasing closer.
Day 3 — Facing devastation, ending with renewal
Won’t You Be My Neighbor?
- A humane, welcoming opener that centers empathy and social repair.
- Gives the audience emotional trust before the day’s darker middle film.
The Road
- Best placed in the middle because it is the most emotionally severe title in the lineup.
- It sharpens the festival’s crisis dimension so the closing note of hope feels substantial.
Cinema Paradiso
- A strong finale because it celebrates memory, artistic inheritance, and emotional continuity.
- Leaves the audience moved, restored, and connected to cinema itself.
Lineup Balance Check
-   Dramas (3):   Leave No Trace, The Peanut Butter Falcon, The Road
-   Documentaries (2):   Collective, Won’t You Be My Neighbor?
-   Animated (2):   Marcel the Shell with Shoes On, The Secret of Kells
-   Comedy (1):   Hunt for the Wilderpeople
-   International feature (1):   Cinema Paradiso
- Note:   Collective   is also international, but it is counted here under documentary to preserve your category balance.
-   Longest runtime:   124 min
-   Black-and-white films:   0
Curatorial Notes
Tone and audience fit
- All selections are suitable for a   mixed adult audience 18+  .
- The overall rhythm avoids stacking the bleakest films back-to-back.
- Each day follows your requested arc:
-   Inviting opener
-   Heavier middle
-   Energizing close
Context for final curation
- Release years and runtimes can vary slightly by distributor/version, but all listed standard cuts are within your length limit.
- “International feature” is programmed as a distinct featured slot with   Cinema Paradiso   to keep the festival finale broad and celebratory.
